body.statement: If \(0<p_0\le1\), \(0<\mu_n\le1\), \(e_0\le1/2\), \(\rho_0\le1/2\), and \(v_0\le1/2\), then \(P_n^{\mathrm{split}}\in\mathcal M_{2n}\), \(\theta_T=0\), and \(\mu_D=\mu_n\). The allocation is \(a_{1x_1}=a_{2x_2}=1/2\), with all other coordinates zero. Since \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X=x_j,Z=z)=1/8\), \(q_{jx_j}(0)=1/2\), and \[V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}},0)=2\frac{(1/2)^2(1/2)}{n}=\frac1{4n},\qquad T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}})=4n\mu_n^2.\] A CACE displacement \(h\) along the compensated Rademacher route has bounded pairwise observed-law divergence whenever \(n\mu_n^2h^2\) is bounded.
body.justification: The exact membership audit and arithmetic calibrate the smallest collection-only least-favorable family.
body.gap: This is a calibration lemma, not a root novelty claim; it verifies the weak-compliance scale under genuinely legal class constants, including \(0<p_0\le1\).
body.consumer: A two-site planner obtains an explicit benchmark when each site covers only one target cell.
body.proof_tex:
All source observations are iid within blocks and the two blocks are independent by construction. Randomization is independent of \((C,\varepsilon)\), consistency holds, exclusion holds because the potential outcome does not depend on \(z\), and monotonicity holds because \(D_j(1)-D_j(0)=C\ge0\). Both source and target ITT outcome contrasts are zero, whereas both receipt contrasts equal \(\mu_n\). Hence transport and collection support hold, although neither source covers both cells, and
\[
 \mu_Y=0,\qquad \mu_D=\mu_n,\qquad\theta_T=0.
\]
The supported source masses equal one, the propensities equal one half, and source shares equal one half. Thus the restrictions on \(p_0,e_0,\rho_0\) verify the respective assumptions.

At \(\theta=0\), \(Y=1/2+\varepsilon/(2\sqrt2)\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X=x_j,Z=z)=\frac18,\qquad
 q_{jx_j}(0)=\frac{1/8}{1/2}+\frac{1/8}{1/2}=\frac12.
\]
More generally, independence of \(C\) and \(\varepsilon\) gives
\[
 q_{jx_j}(\theta)=\frac12+2\theta^2\mu_n(1-\mu_n)\ge\frac12,
\]
so residual-variance regularity follows from \(v_0\le1/2\). Every member property of \(\mathcal M_{2n}\) has now been checked.

Each target cell has only one covering source, so feasibility forces
\(a_{1x_1}=a_{2x_2}=1/2\) and all other coordinates to vanish. Substitution gives
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}},0)
 =2\frac{(1/2)^2(1/2)}n=\frac1{4n},\qquad
 T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}})=4n\mu_n^2.
\]

For the divergence assertion, let the two outcome support points retain equal baseline probabilities. If \(\mu_n\le1/2\), change the upper-point probability of the complier receipt-zero outcome by \(-t\), and that of the never-taker by \(\mu_nt/(1-\mu_n)\). The control mixture is unchanged exactly, while the treated-arm mean changes by \(\mu_n h\), where \(h=t/\sqrt2\). If \(\mu_n>1/2\), change instead the complier receipt-one probability by \(t\); since \(\mu_n\ge1/2\), the same order bound results. The elementary inequality
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(1/2+t,1/2)\le8t^2\qquad(|t|\le1/4)
\]
then yields, after multiplication over the two blocks,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{n,h}^{\mathrm{split}},P_{n,0}^{\mathrm{split}})
 \le Cn\mu_n^2h^2.
\]
Thus pairwise observed-law divergence is bounded whenever \(n\mu_n^2h^2\) is bounded.
